transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled
pros to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman. President Trump has forced the U.S. ambassador to
Greece to step down. She's a leading figure in the MAGA movement. Kimberly Guilfoyle was previously
engaged to be married to Donald Trump Jr. before their relationship ended. NPR's Michelle Kellerman
says Guilfoyle resigned after published stories about her surfaced alleging improper conduct.
The Wall Street Journal has had a series of recent stories about Guilfoyle. There were
lots of allegations of misconduct, including that she asked a Trump donor for $100,000 to pay off a
credit card bill in exchange for, you know, using her contacts within the administration.
NPR's Michelle Kellerman reporting. Guilfoyle says she will vigorously defend her name and reputation.
Officials in Saudi Arabia say a building owned by the state-owned oil company Aramco was attacked
last night and it caught fire. This happened after Saudi Arabia fired into neighboring Yemen,
targeting fuel sites in areas controlled by Yemen's Houthi rebels. NPR's Eya Betrawi reports.
The Saudi Energy Ministry says an Aramco administrative building was targeted in the
eastern city of the Haran, sparking a fire. It gave no further details. Saudi Arabia's Defense
Ministry meanwhile says it's intercepted a number of Houthi missiles and drones targeting various
cities over the past 24 hours. It comes as Saudi fighter jets targeted Houthi-controlled fuel
sites in Yemen on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia says it targeted these sites because they're used to
support Houthi military operations against the kingdom. The Houthis, who are backed by Iran,
say they too are attacking Saudi energy sites because they fuel the kingdom's attacks on Yemen.
The Houthis have also targeted Saudi airports, killing 20 people last week. President Trump wrote
online the Houthis are "behaving very badly" and trying to drive up oil prices ahead of U.S.
midterm elections. Eya Betrawi, NPR News, Dubai. Cornell University has suspended parties at
fraternity houses for the rest of the academic year. That's among other changes in response to
a student's allegations of gang rape two years ago. NPR's Alyssa Natworney reports. The university
announced a number of changes to strengthen campus safety and better support sexual assault
survivors. In addition to banning all parties and social events at fraternity houses,
the Ivy League school will also hire staff to help students navigate reporting sexual misconduct
and will hire criminal investigators independent of Cornell to investigate allegations of sexual
assault on campus. In a letter to the campus, the school's president Michael Kotlikoff writes,
quote, "Cornell must be a place where safety is not an open question." The changes come amid
continued frustration and protests from students and faculty on the handling of Jane Doe's 2024
case. Alyssa Natworney, NPR News, Ithaca, New York. The government releases its latest report
on consumer prices this morning. Economists are watching rising energy prices. This is NPR.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is going to meet new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham
today in London. This comes as Russia steps up its attacks on Ukraine. Zelensky tells NPR
the White House has threatened to cut off its intelligence sharing with Ukraine. He says the
Trump administration is demanding that Ukraine stop firing long range drones at Russian oil
refineries. President Trump claims Ukraine is driving up the costs of diesel for consumers.
Zelensky says that, in fact, the U.S. war against Iran is doing that.
New research from the A.I. company Anthropik suggests that some A.I. might soon be able to
replicate inside smart devices. NPR's Jeff Brumfield explains. Anthropik warned that A.I.
models could soon spread inside network devices around the house, including smart refrigerators,
televisions, and even robotic vacuum cleaners. Researchers demonstrated such replication inside
some cheap TV boxes and with simulations. The researchers warned A.I. worms would be similar
to existing computer viruses, but they would be more adaptable and could be hard to shut down.
The best defense against A.I. and regular viruses alike? A strong password for every
smart device in your home. Jeff Brumfield, NPR News. The Vatican says Pope Leo is expected to
spend the rest of the week in the hospital. He had part of his lower right lung removed yesterday.
The pontiff's doctors say they discovered he had a common form of lung cancer.
I'm Corva Kuhlman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns as U.S. ambassador to Greece after published misconduct allegations
Saudi Aramco administrative building in eastern city of Dhahran catches fire after reported attack
Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi-controlled fuel sites in Yemen as Houthi missile and drone attacks continue
Cornell University suspends fraternity house parties for rest of year, adds safety and reporting changes
Government to release latest consumer price report amid rising energy prices
Zelensky to meet British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in London as Russia escalates attacks on Ukraine
Anthropic research warns AI worms could spread through smart home devices like TVs and refrigerators
Pope Leo expected to remain hospitalized through week after partial lung removal for lung cancer
